label: rem:deconfinement-golden-threshold
title: Quark-gluon plasma deconfinement as the golden ratio phase transition
html:
Remark. Quark-gluon plasma deconfinement as the golden ratio phase transition

The quark-gluon plasma (QGP) deconfinement transition corresponds to the golden ratio degeneration of the Descartes elliptic curve (golden ratio threshold). Hadrons dissolve into free quarks and gluons.

Deconfinement mechanism. Color confinement in QOU is enforced by the S_5-invariance of the Skein module on Bring's surface (chromaticity). Only S_5-invariant combinations of knots in the three color tubes yield positive \tau-evaluation. This S_5-invariance is a property of the smooth elliptic fiber \mathcal{E}_q. The fiber relates the three color tubes.

At q_{\mathrm{gold}} = 1/\varphi^2 \approx 0.382, the elliptic fiber degenerates. \mathcal{E}_q acquires a node. Two roots of the Weierstrass equation coincide. The three color tubes collapse to a degenerate configuration. At this point:

  1. The S_5 symmetry that enforces color neutrality breaks.
  2. The q-chromaticity gamut expands to fill the entire triangle.
  3. Individual quarks acquire positive probability. They are no longer confined.

This is deconfinement. It is a topological phase transition where the fiber that enforces confinement ceases to exist.

First-order character. The QGP transition in QCD lattice simulations is first-order for three or more light quark flavors. In QOU, the first-order character is visible algebraically.

  1. Discriminant crossing. The discriminant of \mathcal{E}_q crosses zero at q_{\mathrm{gold}}. For q > q_{\mathrm{gold}}, \Delta < 0 (smooth curve, one real component). At q = q_{\mathrm{gold}}, \Delta = 0 (nodal curve). Below, \Delta > 0 (two real components, then degenerate). The topology of the real locus changes discontinuously.
  2. Latent heat. The energy difference between the confined phase and the deconfined phase is finite. In crossing-energy units, the latent heat per baryon is
  \mathcal{L}
   \sim 
  \tfrac{1}{2}(n_+ + n_-)\bigl[(q + q^{-1}) -
  (q_{\mathrm{gold}} + q_{\mathrm{gold}}^{-1})\bigr]

This is nonzero for q \neq q_{\mathrm{gold}}. 3. Order parameter. The order parameter is the j-invariant of the elliptic fiber. j(q) is finite and continuous for q > q_{\mathrm{gold}}. It diverges as q \to q_{\mathrm{gold}} (j \to \infty at the node). The divergence of j signals the breakdown of the elliptic structure. The Polyakov loop jumps from zero (confined) to nonzero (deconfined) at the transition.

Effective q at finite temperature. The physical substrate has q = q_0. Temperature changes the effective crossing energy available to disrupt the Borromean structure. At temperature T, thermal fluctuations supply energy \sim k_B T per degree of freedom. Deconfinement occurs when thermal energy matches the Hopf binding energy per baryon:

  k_B T_c
   \sim 
  |\mathfrak{E}_{\mathrm{cross}}(\mathfrak{p})|
   \sim 
  \tfrac{1}{2}(q + q^{-1}) \cdot n_{\mathrm{link}},

where n_{\mathrm{link}} is the number of Hopf-link crossings in the Borromean triple. The effective q at which the chiral structure of the fiber is thermally disrupted is q_{\mathrm{gold}}.

This identifies the QGP transition temperature with the stability margin:

  \frac{k_B T_c}{\Lambda_{\mathrm{QCD}}}
   \sim 
  \frac{q - q_{\mathrm{gold}}}{q}
  = 
  \frac{q_0 - 0.382}{q_0}
   \approx  0.656.

Golden ratio threshold. The QGP phase transition is not at a new scale or coupling constant. It is the same golden ratio that appears in the chiral degeneration, the Penrose tiling, and the E_8 McKay correspondence. Its appearance as the deconfinement boundary is forced by the S_5 symmetry of Bring's surface. The minimal polynomial s^2 + s - 1 = 0 governs both the chiral fiber structure and the confinement mechanism. When the fiber degenerates, confinement breaks.

Phase diagram.

q_{\mathrm{eff}} Phase Fiber Color Hadrons
q > 1 (low T) Confined hadronic Smooth, \Delta < 0 Confined (S_5-inv only) Stable baryons, mesons
q_{\mathrm{gold}} < q < 1 Intermediate Smooth, \Delta > 0 Partially confined Unstable resonances
q = q_{\mathrm{gold}} Critical Nodal Deconfining QGP onset
q < q_{\mathrm{gold}} Deconfined QGP Degenerate Free quarks No stable hadrons
